questions.question: Which of the following statements best links a current conservation initiative for the Great Indian Bustard with its geographical location?

options.text: National Avian Research Centre in Maharashtra conducted habitat simulation for GIB.
Kalyan Sanctuary in Karnataka now houses the largest wild GIB population.
India's first successful artificial insemination of GIB took place in the National Breeding Centre in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan.
A GIB conservation breeding centre was set up in Kutch, Gujarat for desert climate adaptation.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India's first successful artificial insemination of GIB took place in the National Breeding Centre in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Great Indian Bustard (GIB) is critically endangered and is primarily found in the **Thar Desert region of Rajasthan**.
 
• The **National Breeding Centre for GIB** in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan, was established as part of a conservation program to prevent the species from extinction.
 
• In 2020, India's first successful artificial insemination of a GIB was achieved at the breeding center, marking a significant milestone in the conservation of the species.
 
• This initiative is part of a larger effort under the **‘Habitat Improvement and Conservation Breeding of Great Indian Bustard’** project funded by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC).
 
• The breeding center aims to increase GIB population by ensuring successful reproduction under controlled conditions and eventual release into the wild.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Great Indian Bustard (GIB) Overview**

 
 
• The GIB is one of the heaviest flying birds in the world, listed as **Critically Endangered** by the IUCN Red List.
 
• It is native to the Indian subcontinent, with its largest population in Rajasthan.
 
• Key threats include habitat destruction, poaching, and collisions with power lines.
 
 
 
• **Conservation Breeding**
 
 
• Conservation breeding involves captive breeding of species to restore declining populations.
 
• This approach is particularly useful for species like GIB that face high mortality in the wild.
 
 
 
• **Thar Desert Ecosystem**
 
 
• The Thar Desert, also known as the Great Indian Desert, is a key habitat for GIB.
 
• It is characterized by arid conditions, sparse vegetation, and a unique ecosystem that supports several endemic species.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives for GIB Conservation**
 
 
• The **National Wildlife Action Plan (2017-2031)** includes specific actions for GIB conservation.
 
• The **‘Project Great Indian Bustard’** was launched to mitigate threats like habitat loss and power line collisions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Metals** conduct electricity through **free electrons**, which move under the influence of an electric field, making them good conductors.
 
• An **ionised gas (plasma)** conducts via **electrons and positively charged ions**, as both species act as mobile charge carriers.
 
• **Electrolytes** such as acids, bases, and salts conduct current by movement of **positive (cations) and negative (anions)** ions in solution.
 
• This classification shows how different materials rely on different **mobile charge carriers** for conduction: electrons, ions, or both.
 
• The correct mapping is: **A–3 (Metal–Electrons), B–2 (Ionised gas–Electrons & Positive Ions), C–1 (Electrolyte–Positive & Negative Ions)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Conduction in Metals**

 
 
• Follows the **electron sea model**, where delocalised electrons move freely.
 
• Examples: copper, silver, and aluminium—excellent conductors due to high electron density.
 
 
 
• **Conduction in Ionised Gas (Plasma)**
 
 
• Plasma is called the **fourth state of matter**.
 
• Electricity conduction occurs due to **free electrons and ions** created by ionisation.
 
• Examples: fluorescent lamps, auroras, lightning.
 
 
 
• **Conduction in Electrolytes**
 
 
• Electrolytes dissociate into **ions in solution** (e.g., NaCl → Na⁺ + Cl⁻).
 
• Used in **batteries, electrolysis, and biological systems**.
 
 
 
• **Key Concept**
 
 
• The type of **mobile charge carrier** determines the mechanism of current flow.
 
• Solids (metals) → electrons, Liquids (electrolytes) → ions, Gases (plasma) → ions + electrons.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct? 

(1) Birth rate measures the number of children born per 1000 people annually.

(2) Pull factors include opportunities that attract people to new regions.

(3) Death rate is always higher than birth rate.

(4) Push factors can include civil unrest and lack of jobs.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1, 2, and 4 only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Birth rate** refers to the number of live births per 1,000 people in a population per year. This is a key demographic indicator.
 
• **Pull factors** are conditions or opportunities (e.g., jobs, better living standards, education) that attract individuals to migrate to a particular area.
 
• The statement “Death rate is always higher than birth rate” is incorrect. In many cases, especially in developing countries, the birth rate is higher than the death rate.
 
• **Push factors** are adverse conditions such as civil unrest, unemployment, or environmental disasters that drive people to leave their homes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Demographic Indicators:**

 
 
• Demographic indicators like birth rate, death rate, and migration rates are essential for understanding population trends.
 
• These indicators influence government policies on healthcare, education, housing, and employment.
 
 
 
• **Migration Push and Pull Factors:**
 
 
• **Push factors:** Include poverty, political instability, natural disasters, and lack of opportunities.
 
• **Pull factors:** Include better employment opportunities, healthcare, education, and higher quality of life.
 
 
 
• **Population Growth Dynamics:**
 
 
• Population growth depends on the difference between birth and death rates, along with migration.
 
• In developing countries, high birth rates are often coupled with declining death rates due to improved healthcare.
 
 
 
• **Global Trends:**
 
 
• Developed nations typically have low birth and death rates, leading to stable or declining populations.
 
• Developing nations often experience high birth rates and declining death rates, leading to rapid population growth.

questions.question: What does the term ‘capital formation’ refer to in macroeconomics?

options.text: Growth in production capacity through investment

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Growth in production capacity through investment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Capital formation** in macroeconomics refers to the process of increasing the stock of physical and human capital in an economy through investment.
 
• It involves the allocation of resources to create infrastructure, machinery, tools, and other assets that enhance production capacity.
 
• Investment in capital formation is crucial for economic growth, as it raises productivity and facilitates the production of goods and services.
 
• Capital formation can be categorized into physical capital (e.g., factories, equipment) and human capital (e.g., education, training).
 
• This process is typically driven by savings, investments, and financial intermediation within the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Physical Capital**

 
 
• Refers to tangible assets like machinery, buildings, and infrastructure that aid in production.
 
• Physical capital is considered a key factor in increasing an economy's output and efficiency.
 
 
 
• **Human Capital**
 
 
• Refers to the skills, knowledge, and expertise of the workforce.
 
• Investment in education and training improves human capital, leading to higher productivity.
 
 
 
• **Savings and Investment**
 
 
• Savings are essential for capital formation, as they provide the funds needed for investment.
 
• Higher savings rates in an economy generally lead to increased levels of investment.
 
 
 
• **Role of Financial Institutions**
 
 
• Financial institutions like banks and capital markets play a critical role in channeling savings into investments.
 
• They act as intermediaries, ensuring efficient allocation of funds for productive purposes.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Economic Growth**
 
 
• Capital formation boosts production and generates employment, leading to sustained economic growth.
 
• It helps economies transition from lower-income to higher-income stages over time.

questions.question: Which of the following North-Eastern states has areas governed under the Sixth Schedule?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tripura**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the administration of tribal areas in four North-Eastern states: **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram**.
 
• Tripura has areas governed under the Sixth Schedule, specifically the **Tripura Tribal Areas Autonomous District Council (TTAADC)**.
 
• The Sixth Schedule provides for the creation of Autonomous District Councils (ADCs) to preserve the rights, customs, and identity of tribal communities.
 
• The ADCs have legislative, judicial, and executive powers, including control over land, forests, and village administration in tribal areas.
 
• Tripura's tribal areas constitute about **68% of the state's total geographical area**, making the Sixth Schedule crucial for governance there.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sixth Schedule:**

 
 
• Introduced to protect the cultural and economic interests of the tribal communities in select areas.
 
• Applies to certain areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram.
 
• Provides for decentralization through Autonomous District and Regional Councils.
 
• Empowers these councils to make laws on land, forests, agriculture, customs, and other local matters.
 
 
 
• **Tripura Tribal Areas Autonomous District Council (TTAADC):**
 
 
• Established in 1985 under the Sixth Schedule.
 
• Covers tribal-dominated areas of Tripura.
 
• Ensures protection of tribal rights and self-governance.
 
 
 
• **Other North-Eastern States:**
 
 
• Manipur and Arunachal Pradesh are not governed under the Sixth Schedule.
 
• Nagaland has special provisions under Article 371A, but not the Sixth Schedule.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Sixth Schedule:**
 
 
• Preserves tribal culture, traditions, and autonomy in governance.
 
• Promotes development while ensuring tribal identity is not diluted.

questions.question: What is the punishment for abetment of an offense under the POCSO Act?

options.text: Half the punishment prescribed for the offense

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Same punishment as the offense**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offenses (POCSO) Act, abetment of an offense is treated with the **same punishment as the offense itself.**
 
• The Act ensures stringent penalties for individuals who aid, encourage, or facilitate the commission of sexual offenses against children.
 
• Abetment is broadly defined to include instigating, engaging in conspiracy, or intentionally aiding the offense, highlighting the comprehensive nature of the Act.
 
• POCSO provides legal protection to children (individuals below 18 years of age) against a wide range of sexual offenses, including abetment.
 
• These provisions aim to strengthen the deterrence against child abuse and ensure accountability for all parties involved.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **POCSO Act Overview:**

 
 
• The POCSO Act was enacted in 2012 to address child sexual abuse comprehensively.
 
• It defines offenses such as penetrative sexual assault, non-penetrative sexual assault, sexual harassment, and pornography involving children.
 
• The Act makes it mandatory to report offenses and prescribes penalties for failure to do so.
 
 
 
• **Abetment Under Indian Penal Code (IPC):**
 
 
• In the IPC, abetment refers to instigating, conspiring, or aiding the commission of an offense.
 
• The POCSO Act builds upon IPC provisions to ensure specific protections for children.
 
 
 
• **Child-Friendly Procedures:**
 
 
• The POCSO Act mandates child-friendly procedures during investigation and trial, such as avoiding direct confrontation with the accused.
 
• It ensures the confidentiality of the victim and provides assistance through special educators or interpreters.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Interpretation:**
 
 
• Indian courts have consistently reinforced strict adherence to POCSO provisions, emphasizing punishment for abetment.
 
• Judgments highlight the importance of protecting the vulnerable sections of society, especially children.

questions.question: Which layer of the Earth's atmosphere is primarily responsible for absorbing ultraviolet radiation from the Sun?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Stratosphere**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Stratosphere is the second layer of Earth's atmosphere, located above the Troposphere and below the Mesosphere.
 
• It contains the **ozone layer**, which plays a vital role in absorbing the majority of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation.
 
• The ozone layer is concentrated between 15 to 35 kilometers above Earth's surface within the Stratosphere.
 
• Ultraviolet radiation absorption by ozone molecules prevents excessive UV exposure on Earth's surface, protecting living organisms from DNA damage.
 
• Human activities, such as the release of chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), have historically caused damage to the ozone layer, leading to international agreements like the **Montreal Protocol** to phase out ozone-depleting substances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ozone Layer:**

 
 
• Ozone is a molecule composed of three oxygen atoms (O₃).
 
• It is formed naturally through the interaction of ultraviolet light with oxygen molecules (O₂) in the Stratosphere.
 
• The ozone layer absorbs UV-B and UV-C radiation, while allowing UV-A radiation to pass through.
 
 
 
• **Atmospheric Layers:**
 
 
• The Earth's atmosphere is divided into five main layers: Troposphere, Stratosphere, Mesosphere, Thermosphere, and Exosphere.
 
• The Troposphere is the lowest layer, where weather occurs, while the Stratosphere is above it and houses the ozone layer.
 
• The Mesosphere is known for meteoroid burning, and the Thermosphere includes the ionosphere, crucial for radio communication.
 
 
 
• **Ultraviolet Radiation:**
 
 
• UV radiation is part of the electromagnetic spectrum emitted by the Sun.
 
• It is classified into three types: UV-A, UV-B, and UV-C based on wavelength.
 
• Excessive UV exposure can cause skin cancer, cataracts, and immune system suppression in humans.
 
 
 
• **Montreal Protocol:**
 
 
• Signed in 1987, this international treaty aims to phase out the production and consumption of ozone-depleting substances.
 
• It has been highly successful in reducing chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) and other harmful chemicals, aiding in ozone layer recovery.
 
• The protocol is considered one of the most effective environmental treaties globally.

questions.question: In the context of Mughal administration, who were referred to as Shaikhzadas or Hindustanis?

options.text: Central Asian nobles of Turkic origin serving the Mughals
Rajput converts elevated to noble ranks for loyalty
Persian-trained officers recruited from Safavid Iran
Indigenous Muslims who held administrative posts under Mughal rule

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indigenous Muslims who held administrative posts under Mughal rule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Shaikhzadas or Hindustanis referred to **indigenous Muslims**, primarily those who were born in India and held administrative roles in the Mughal Empire.
 
• They were distinct from the **foreign-born nobles** such as Persians, Afghans, or Central Asians who also served the Mughal court.
 
• This group formed a significant part of the Mughal bureaucracy and contributed to the **stability and governance** of the empire.
 
• The term "Hindustanis" emphasized their regional association with the Indian subcontinent, distinguishing them from immigrant elites.
 
• Shaikhzadas often acted as a **bridging community** between the Mughal rulers and the local populace, facilitating smoother administration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nobility in Mughal Administration:**

 
 
• The Mughal nobility was a mix of ethnic groups, including **Persians, Turks, Afghans, and Hindustanis**.
 
• They were ranked based on the **mansabdari system**, which determined their military and administrative responsibilities.
 
• The mansabdars were categorized into **zat (personal rank) and sawar (cavalry rank).**
 
 
 
• **Central Asian Nobles:**
 
 
• These were elites of **Turkic or Timurid origin** who migrated from regions such as Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan.
 
• They played a critical role in the early Mughal conquests and administration.
 
 
 
• **Persian Influence:**
 
 
• Persian culture and language heavily influenced the Mughal court.
 
• Many Persian-trained officers were recruited due to their **expertise in governance and military strategy.**
 
 
 
• **Rajput and Hindu Nobles:**
 
 
• The Mughal emperors, especially Akbar, allied with Rajput rulers, integrating them into the Mughal nobility.
 
• This policy helped in **reducing resistance** and strengthening the empire.
 
 
 
• **Role of Indigenous Muslims:**
 
 
• Indigenous Muslims or Shaikhzadas were crucial for local administration and revenue collection.
 
• Their deep understanding of local conditions enhanced the efficiency of the Mughal governance system.

questions.question: Which of the following bodies has the power to create new All-India Services common to both the Union and the States?

options.text: The President of India by issuing an executive order.
The Union Cabinet by a simple majority.
The Prime Minister with the consent of all Chief Ministers.
The Parliament, provided the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by a special majority.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Parliament, provided the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by a special majority**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The creation of new All-India Services common to both the Union and the States requires a **special resolution passed by the Rajya Sabha**, as per Article 312 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Such a resolution must be supported by a **two-thirds majority of members present and voting** in the Rajya Sabha.
 
• Once the resolution is passed, **Parliament gains legislative authority** to enact laws for the establishment of the new All-India Service.
 
• All-India Services include existing services like the **Indian Administrative Service (IAS)**, **Indian Police Service (IPS)**, and the **Indian Forest Service (IFS)**.
 
• The Rajya Sabha's special role reflects the federal structure of India, ensuring that states have representation in decisions affecting shared administrative services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 312 of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• This article empowers the Parliament to create new All-India Services if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution to that effect.
 
• It ensures coordination between the Union and the States in key administrative functions.
 
 
 
• **All-India Services:**
 
 
• The All-India Services are unique to India's federal structure, where officers serve both the Union and State governments.
 
• These services ensure uniformity in administrative practices across the country.
 
 
 
• **Special Majority:**
 
 
• A special majority requires the support of at least two-thirds of the members present and voting.
 
• This ensures that major decisions have widespread support in the legislative body.
 
 
 
• **Rajya Sabha's Role:**
 
 
• The Rajya Sabha (Council of States) represents the states in India's federal structure.
 
• Its special role in creating All-India Services underscores the importance of states in the decision-making process.

 Before becoming the Governor, he was a **senior bureaucrat** and served as the **Secretary, Department of Financial Services (DFS)** in the Government of India.

questions.question: Which is the largest island of India in terms of area?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Great Nicobar Island**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Great Nicobar Island** is the largest island in India in terms of area, covering approximately **921 square kilometers**.
 
• It is part of the Nicobar Islands, which are located in the southeastern region of the **Andaman and Nicobar Islands Union Territory**.
 
• The island is known for its diverse flora and fauna, including the famous **Nicobar megapode**, a rare bird species endemic to the region.
 
• Great Nicobar Island is home to the **Indira Point**, the southernmost point of India.
 
• The region is sparsely populated and primarily inhabited by the indigenous Shompen tribe and Nicobarese people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Andaman and Nicobar Islands:**

 
 
• The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are a group of 572 islands located at the juncture of the Bay of Bengal and the Andaman Sea.
 
• The islands are divided into two main groups: the Andaman Islands and the Nicobar Islands.
 
• The archipelago is known for its pristine beaches, coral reefs, and tropical rainforests.
 
 
 
• **Indira Point:**
 
 
• Indira Point is the southernmost tip of India, located on Great Nicobar Island.
 
• It was formerly known as Parsons Point and was renamed in honor of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.
 
• Indira Point was submerged during the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami, causing significant geographical changes in the area.
 
 
 
• **Shompen Tribe:**
 
 
• The Shompen are one of the oldest and most isolated tribes of the Nicobar Islands.
 
• They practice a hunter-gatherer lifestyle and are considered a Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG).
 
• Their population is concentrated in the interior regions of Great Nicobar Island.
 
 
 
• **Biodiversity in Great Nicobar:**
 
 
• Great Nicobar Island is part of the UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves.
 
• The island is home to unique species such as the Nicobar crab-eating macaque and saltwater crocodiles.
 
• The Great Nicobar Biosphere Reserve ensures the protection of its rich ecosystem.

questions.question: Where was the National shooting Championship 2024 held?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The National Shooting Championship 2024 was held in **Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh**, a prominent location for hosting sports events in India.
 
• This championship is one of the most prestigious events for Indian shooters and serves as a platform to identify and nurture talent for international competitions.
 
• Bhopal has emerged as a significant center for national-level sports events, with its modern infrastructure and facilities.
 
• The championship features various categories, including rifle, pistol, and shotgun events, catering to athletes from across the country.
 
• The event is organized under the aegis of the **National Rifle Association of India (NRAI)**, the governing body for shooting sports in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Rifle Association of India (NRAI):**

 
 
• Established in 1951, NRAI is the governing body for shooting sports in India.
 
• It is affiliated with the International Shooting Sport Federation (ISSF) and represents India in global shooting events.
 
• NRAI works to promote the sport of shooting and support athletes with training and resources.
 
 
 
• **Shooting Sports in India:**
 
 
• Shooting is one of India's most successful sports in international competitions, including the Olympics, Commonwealth Games, and Asian Games.
 
• Prominent Indian shooters include Abhinav Bindra, Gagan Narang, and Manu Bhaker, who have brought laurels to the country.
 
• The sport is categorized into rifle, pistol, and shotgun events, with further subdivisions based on distance and targets.
 
 
 
• **Facilities in Bhopal:**
 
 
• The city is equipped with state-of-the-art sports facilities, including shooting ranges that meet international standards.
 
• Bhopal's infrastructure supports large-scale events, making it a preferred choice for national sports championships.
 
 
 
• **Significance of National Shooting Championship:**
 
 
• It serves as a selection event for international competitions, including the Olympics and World Championships.
 
• The championship fosters healthy competition among athletes and provides them with exposure to high-pressure situations.
 
• It also encourages young talent to take up shooting as a professional sport.

questions.question: Which of the following is correctly matched with their leadership role in the Constituent Assembly (During the making of the Indian constitution)?

options.text: G.V. Mavalankar - Chairman of the Committee on the Functions of the Constituent Assembly
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar - Head of the Committee on the Functions of the Assembly
N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar - Chairman of the Order of Business Committee
K.M. Munshi-Leader of the Committee on Fundamental Rights

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**G.V. Mavalankar - Chairman of the Committee on the Functions of the Constituent Assembly**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **G.V. Mavalankar**, a prominent figure in the Constituent Assembly, served as the Chairman of the Committee on the Functions of the Constituent Assembly.
 
• The Committee was responsible for laying down the procedural framework for the Constituent Assembly.
 
• Mavalankar also played a significant role as the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha post-independence, showcasing his leadership capabilities.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a monument with its architectural style?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Qutub Minar**, located in Delhi, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the finest examples of Indo-Islamic architecture.
 
• It was initiated by Qutb-ud-din Aibak in 1192 and completed by Iltutmish, reflecting the architectural blend of Islamic and Indian styles.
 
• The tower is primarily constructed from red sandstone, with intricate carvings of Arabic inscriptions and geometric patterns, showcasing Islamic artistry.
 
• Its tapering structure stands at a height of approximately 73 meters and consists of five distinct storeys.
 
• The Qutub Minar is surrounded by other historically significant structures, such as the Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque and the Iron Pillar, adding to its cultural importance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indo-Islamic Architecture:**

 
 
• A distinctive blend of Indian and Islamic architectural styles that emerged during the medieval period in India.
 
• Features include domes, minarets, arches, intricate calligraphy, and geometric patterns, often combined with Indian motifs like lotus and floral designs.
 
• Prominent examples include Qutub Minar, Taj Mahal, and Humayun's Tomb.
 
 
 
• **Qutb-ud-din Aibak:**
 
 
• Founder of the Delhi Sultanate and the first ruler of the Slave Dynasty.
 
• Initiated the construction of Qutub Minar as a victory tower to commemorate his conquest of Delhi.
 
 
 
• **Iron Pillar at Qutub Complex:**
 
 
• Located near Qutub Minar, it is a 7-meter-high pillar made of wrought iron and dates back to the Gupta period.
 
• Known for its rust-resistant composition, it is a marvel of ancient Indian metallurgy.
 
 
 
• **Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque:**
 
 
• Situated within the Qutub Complex, it is one of the earliest mosques built in India.
 
• Constructed using materials from 27 demolished Hindu and Jain temples, showcasing the amalgamation of cultural influences.

questions.question: What is the radius of the centre circle in a football field?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**9.15 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The radius of the center circle in a standard football field is **9.15 meters**, as per FIFA Laws of the Game.
 
• The center circle is used during kick-off to ensure that the opposing team maintains a minimum distance of **9.15 meters** from the ball.
 
• The center circle is marked around the center spot, which is located at the midpoint of the halfway line of the field.
 
• This measurement ensures uniformity across official football fields worldwide for fair gameplay.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **FIFA Laws of the Game:**

 
 
• The Laws of the Game are the set of rules codified by FIFA, governing the play of football globally.
 
• Law 1 outlines the dimensions and markings of the field, including the center circle.
 
 
 
• **Purpose of the Center Circle:**
 
 
• The center circle ensures players of the opposing team maintain a minimum distance from the ball during kick-off.
 
• This rule promotes fair play and reduces interference during the game's start or after a goal.
 
 
 
• **Other Standard Dimensions:**
 
 
• The penalty area is 16.5 m from the goal line and extends 16.5 m on either side of the goal.
 
• The goal area is 5.5 m from the goal line and 5.5 m from each goalpost.
 
 
 
• **Regulations for Markings:**
 
 
• The field must be rectangular, with touchlines longer than the goal lines.
 
• All markings must be clear, typically in white, and follow the dimensions specified by FIFA.

questions.question: According to the Constitution of India, what is the quorum required to constitute a meeting of either House of Parliament?

options.text: One-third of the total number of members of the House.
Fifty members in the Lok Sabha and twenty-five members in the Rajya Sabha.
One-tenth of the total number of members of the House.
One-fourth of the total number of members of the House.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**One-tenth of the total number of members of the House**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per Article 100(3) of the Constitution of India, the quorum required to conduct meetings of either House of Parliament is **one-tenth of the total number of members of the House**.
 
• The term "quorum" refers to the minimum number of members that must be present for the proceedings of a legislative body to be valid.
 
• If the quorum is not met, the meeting of the House cannot proceed, and it may be adjourned.
 
• The quorum ensures effective participation and functioning of the legislative process, preventing decisions being made by an insufficient number of members.
 
• This provision applies to both the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, ensuring consistency in parliamentary practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 100 of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• It deals with voting in Houses, quorum, and the validity of proceedings.
 
• Clause (3) specifically mentions the quorum requirement as one-tenth of the total members.
 
 
 
• **Lok Sabha:**
 
 
• The Lok Sabha is the lower house of India's Parliament and consists of 543 elected members.
 
• For a quorum in Lok Sabha, at least 55 members must be present.
 
 
 
• **Rajya Sabha:**
 
 
• The Rajya Sabha is the upper house of India's Parliament and has a maximum strength of 250 members.
 
• For a quorum in Rajya Sabha, at least 25 members must be present.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Quorum:**
 
 
• It prevents decision-making by an unrepresentative minority.
 
• Ensures a fair and democratic legislative process.
 
 
 
• **Adjournment Due to Lack of Quorum:**
 
 
• If the quorum is not met, the Speaker or Chairman may adjourn the session until the required number of members are present.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the main objective of the Indo-French Megha-Tropiques satellite mission?

options.text: Understanding convective systems and the water cycle in tropical regions
Studying polar ice melt and its impact on global sea levels
Mapping mineral resources in the Himalayan region
Monitoring ozone depletion over the equator

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indo-French Megha-Tropiques satellite mission aims to study **convective systems, the water cycle, and energy exchanges in tropical regions**.
 
• It was launched on **12 October 2011** by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) in collaboration with the French space agency CNES.
 
• The satellite carries four advanced instruments—SAPHIR, SCARAB, MADRAS, and ROSA—to monitor precipitation, atmospheric humidity, and radiation in tropical areas.
 
• Megha-Tropiques is particularly designed to gather **data for climate and weather predictions**, focusing on tropical cyclones, monsoons, and extreme weather events.
 
• The satellite contributes significantly to global climate studies by providing **high-resolution and frequent observations** of the tropics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Convective Systems:**

 
 
• Convective systems are large-scale atmospheric phenomena that involve the vertical movement of air masses.
 
• They play a crucial role in the **formation of clouds, precipitation, and weather patterns**.
 
• Studying these systems aids in understanding **monsoon dynamics and climate variability**.
 
 
 
• **Tropical Water Cycle:**
 
 
• The tropical water cycle involves processes like evaporation, condensation, and precipitation, which are **essential for sustaining ecosystems**.
 
• Data from Megha-Tropiques helps in analyzing how water vapor contributes to **heat transfer and energy balance** in the atmosphere.
 
 
 
• **Instruments on Megha-Tropiques:**
 
 
• **SAPHIR:** Measures humidity profiles in the atmosphere.
 
• **SCARAB:** Monitors Earth's radiation budget.
 
• **MADRAS:** Tracks rainfall and cloud properties.
 
• **ROSA:** Observes GPS signals for atmospheric studies.
 
 
 
• **Significance for Global Climate Studies:**
 
 
• Megha-Tropiques contributes to global satellite-based climate monitoring efforts like **GEWEX (Global Energy and Water Exchanges)**.
 
• Its data is used by **meteorological agencies worldwide** to improve weather forecasting and climate modeling.

questions.question: The regulatory framework adopted by India between 1947 and 1990, often referred to as the "License Raj," aimed to direct economic activity. While it had certain intended benefits, what was a significant unintended negative consequence often associated with this system?

options.text: The creation of barriers to entry for new businesses potentially stifling innovation and leading to inefficiencies.
A significant reduction in corruption and bureaucratic delays in obtaining necessary approvals for economic activities.
A rapid increase in the quality and global competitiveness of Indian-made goods due to stringent quality control measures.
The fostering of a highly competitive market environment with numerous players in each industry.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The creation of barriers to entry for new businesses potentially stifling innovation and leading to inefficiencies.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The License Raj system mandated **strict licensing and regulations** for businesses, which often resulted in bureaucratic hurdles for entrepreneurs.
 
• This framework created significant **barriers to entry** for new businesses, discouraging competition and innovation in the economy.
 
• The over-reliance on government approvals led to **inefficiencies**, as companies had to navigate a complex web of red tape.
 
• Monopolistic tendencies emerged as **established players dominated industries**, reducing the scope for new entrants and innovation.
 
• The lack of a competitive environment resulted in **low-quality goods** and services, impacting India's global trade and industrial development during the period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **License Raj:**

 
 
• It refers to the system of elaborate licenses, regulations, and accompanying red tape required to set up and run businesses in India.
 
• Introduced post-independence to promote self-reliance and prevent foreign domination of Indian industries.
 
• While aiming to protect domestic industries, it inadvertently stifled growth and innovation.
 
 
 
• **Economic Consequences:**
 
 
• Resulted in significant delays for businesses due to the long bureaucratic approval process.
 
• Limited foreign investment, further reducing access to advanced technologies and global practices.
 
 
 
• **Innovation Stagnation:**
 
 
• Entrepreneurs faced challenges entering the market, which slowed down industrial innovation.
 
• Industries largely focused on meeting government quotas rather than improving quality or efficiency.
 
 
 
• **Post-1991 Reforms:**
 
 
• India's economic liberalization in 1991 marked a shift away from the License Raj.
 
• Reforms included deregulation, reduction of trade barriers, and promotion of foreign investments to address inefficiencies.

questions.question: Which classical dance form originated in Andhra Pradesh and incorporates both singing and dancing?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kuchipudi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kuchipudi** is a classical dance form that originated in Andhra Pradesh, India.
 
• It is distinctive as it combines **singing and dancing**, making it unique among Indian classical dance styles.
 
• The dance form derives its name from **Kuchipudi village** in Krishna district, Andhra Pradesh.
 
• Kuchipudi performances are often based on **Hindu religious themes**, particularly stories from epics like the Ramayana and Mahabharata.
 
• It involves elaborate **expressions (Abhinaya)**, intricate footwork, and rhythmic patterns, showcasing both grace and technical skill.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **History of Kuchipudi:**

 
 
• Kuchipudi traces its origins to the **Bhakti movement** and was traditionally performed by male Brahmin performers called Bhagavatulu.
 
• The dance form was formalized in the 17th century by **Siddhendra Yogi**, a renowned saint and scholar.
 
• Initially, Kuchipudi was performed in temples as a way to narrate mythological stories and glorify deities.
 
 
 
• **Performance Style:**
 
 
• Kuchipudi integrates **dialogues, music, and dance**, often performed in groups or solo acts.
 
• It employs intricate hand gestures (**Mudras**) and facial expressions to convey emotions and stories.
 
• The dance has a unique feature called **Tarangam**, where the performer dances on a brass plate with precision and balance.
 
 
 
• **Music and Costumes:**
 
 
• The music for Kuchipudi is predominantly **Carnatic**, with lyrics in Telugu or Sanskrit.
 
• The costumes are vibrant, featuring traditional silk attire with intricate embellishments, complemented by jewelry and makeup.
 
 
 
• **Global Recognition:**
 
 
• Kuchipudi has gained international acclaim and is performed worldwide by artists trained in this classical art form.
 
• It is recognized as one of the eight major classical dance forms of India by the **Sangeet Natak Akademi**.

questions.question: Ganesh Chaturthi, celebrated widely in Maharashtra, is associated with:

__
 
• Ganesh Chaturthi is a Hindu festival celebrated to mark the **birth of Lord Ganesha**, the deity of wisdom, prosperity, and good fortune.
 
• It is observed in the **Bhadrapada month** of the Hindu calendar, typically in August or September.
 
• The festival lasts for **10 days**, culminating in the immersion (visarjan) of Ganesha idols in water bodies.
 
• Maharashtra is known for its grand and elaborate celebrations, with public installations of **large Ganesha idols** and cultural events.
 
• The festival was popularized in the 19th century by freedom fighter **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** to unite people during the Indian independence movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Lord Ganesha is considered the **remover of obstacles** and is worshipped before undertaking any new venture.
 
• He is the son of **Lord Shiva** and **Goddess Parvati**.
 
• His iconic attributes include an **elephant head**, a trunk, and a pot-bellied body, symbolizing wisdom and prosperity.
 
 
 
• **Visarjan (Immersion):**
 
 
• The immersion of Ganesha idols signifies the cycle of creation and dissolution in nature.
 
• Eco-friendly idols made of biodegradable materials are increasingly used to prevent water pollution.
 
 
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak's Role:**
 
 
• Tilak transformed Ganesh Chaturthi into a **community festival** to foster unity and cultural pride during British colonial rule.
 
• Public celebrations helped unite people across social and economic barriers.
 
 
 
• **Regional Significance:**
 
 
• While Maharashtra is famous for its Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations, states like **Karnataka, Goa, and Andhra Pradesh** also observe the festival with zeal.
 
• Different regions have unique rituals and cultural performances associated with the festival.

• **Legal Protection:**
 
 
• GI registration provides legal protection to the product, preventing misuse by unauthorized producers.

__
 
• North Korea withdrew from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) in **2003**, marking a significant step toward its nuclear weapons development.
 
• The decision to withdraw was in response to North Korea’s claims of U.S. aggression and alleged violations of agreements.

• The NPT is an international treaty aimed at preventing the spread of nuclear weapons and promoting peaceful uses of nuclear energy.
 
• It came into force in **1970** and currently has **191 member states**.
 
• Countries that possess nuclear weapons under the treaty include the U.S., Russia, China, France, and the U.K.
 
• North Korea initially joined the NPT in **1985** but later withdrew in **2003**.
 
 
 
• **North Korea's Nuclear Program**
 
 
• North Korea's nuclear ambitions date back to the **1960s**, with assistance from Soviet-era technology.
 
• The program intensified after the collapse of the Soviet Union and North Korea's withdrawal from the NPT.
 
• North Korea has conducted multiple nuclear tests, with the most recent being in **2017**.

• The sanctions target sectors like arms trade, fuel imports, and luxury goods to curb its nuclear program.
 
• Despite sanctions, North Korea has continued its missile development and nuclear testing.
 
 
 
• **Impact of North Korea's Nuclear Program**
 
 
• North Korea's nuclear program has heightened tensions in East Asia, especially with South Korea, Japan, and the U.S.
 
• It has prompted calls for diplomatic solutions, including denuclearization talks, though progress has been limited.
 
• The program continues to be a major challenge for global nuclear non-proliferation efforts.

options.text: Both A and R are false

questions.solution:

• **Reason (R)** is true because these platforms were indeed found to contain traces of wheat and barley grains, indicating their association with storage or processing activities rather than religious purposes.
 
• Harappan civilization was primarily urban, and its structures often had practical purposes such as granaries, workshops, or drainage systems rather than religious use.
 
• The presence of grains like wheat and barley aligns with the agricultural economy of the Harappans, which was a key aspect of their livelihood.
 
• Thus, the correct conclusion is that A is false, but R is true, as the Reason (R) does not support the Assertion (A).

• **Harappan Civilization:**

 
 
• It is also known as the Indus Valley Civilization, flourishing between 2500 BCE and 1900 BCE.
 
• Prominent sites include Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, Dholavira, Kalibangan, and Lothal.
 
• The civilization was known for advanced urban planning, drainage systems, and standardized weights and measures.
 
 
 
• **Granaries in Harappa:**
 
 
• Large granaries were discovered at Harappa and Mohenjo-daro, indicating surplus food production and storage.
 
• These granaries were often located near river banks for easy transport of goods.
 
 
 
• **Agriculture in Harappan Society:**

questions.question: The Alaknanda River originates from which of the following?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The Alaknanda River originates from the **Satopanth Glacier**, which is located near the base of the Chaukhamba peaks in the Uttarakhand region of India.
 
• Satopanth Glacier is situated at an altitude of approximately **7,000 meters above sea level**.
 
• The glacier feeds the Alaknanda River, one of the two main tributaries that combine to form the Ganga River.
 
• The Alaknanda River meets the Bhagirathi River at **Devprayag**, where it officially takes the name "Ganga."
 
• Satopanth Glacier is a popular trekking destination and holds religious significance in Hindu mythology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Satopanth Glacier**

 
 
• It is named after "Satopanth," a Sanskrit word meaning "True Path."
 
• It lies in the **Garhwal region** of Uttarakhand, India, and is surrounded by peaks such as Chaukhamba, Neelkanth, and Balakun.
 
• Satopanth Glacier is a vital source of freshwater and plays a crucial role in the hydrology of the Ganga Basin.

• **Ganga River**
 
 
• The Ganga is considered a holy river in India and holds immense cultural, spiritual, and ecological significance.
 
• It is formed by the confluence of the Alaknanda and Bhagirathi rivers at Devprayag.

• These peaks form the westernmost group of the Garhwal Himalayas and are part of the Gangotri Group.
 
• They serve as a prominent landmark near the Satopanth Glacier.

questions.question: What significant Institutional development emerged from banking reforms after 1991 to regulate financial stability?

• The **Board for Financial Supervision (BFS)** was established in 1994 as a committee of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to ensure the soundness of the financial system in India.
 
• BFS functions under the RBI and is tasked with **supervising commercial banks, financial institutions, and non-banking financial companies (NBFCs)**.
 
• The BFS was created as part of the **post-1991 banking reforms** to strengthen financial stability and improve the efficiency of the supervisory framework.
 
• It plays a crucial role in **monitoring systemic risks** and ensuring compliance with prudential regulations in the banking and financial sectors.
 
• BFS has significantly contributed to fostering transparency, accountability, and resilience within India's financial system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Banking Reforms of 1991:**

 
 
• The 1991 reforms were initiated as part of structural adjustments following the **Balance of Payments (BoP) crisis** in India.
 
• Key measures included liberalization, privatization, and globalization to enhance efficiency and competitiveness in the banking sector.
 
• The reforms aimed to reduce non-performing assets (NPAs), improve capital adequacy, and modernize the banking infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Role of RBI in Financial Supervision:**
 
 
• As the central bank, the RBI is responsible for **maintaining monetary stability and regulating banks and NBFCs**.
 
• The establishment of BFS strengthened the RBI's supervisory capacity by providing a focused oversight mechanism.
 
 
 
• **Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs):**
 
 
• NBFCs are financial institutions that provide banking-like services but do not hold a banking license.
 
• They are regulated by the RBI and play a vital role in supporting credit access in sectors underserved by traditional banks.
 
 
 
• **Systemic Risk Management:**
 
 
• Systemic risk refers to the risk of collapse of an entire financial system or market.
 
• The BFS, through its supervisory framework, helps **identify and mitigate such risks** to ensure the stability of the financial ecosystem.

questions.question: Which of the following is a unique characteristic of sponges (Phylum Porifera)?

options.text: Radial symmetry and presence of tentacles

__
 
• Sponges (Phylum Porifera) are characterized by the presence of a **water canal system**, which facilitates water circulation for feeding, respiration, and excretion.
 
• **Choanocytes**, or collar cells, are specialized cells in sponges responsible for creating water currents and trapping food particles.
 
• The water canal system includes structures such as **ostia (pores), spongocoel (central cavity), and osculum (exit opening)**, ensuring efficient water flow.
 
• Sponges lack tissues and organs but have a unique cellular organization that supports their **filter-feeding mechanism**.
 
• They exhibit **asymmetry or radial symmetry**, making them distinct from other animal phyla.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Choanocytes:**

 
 
• These are flagellated cells with a collar-like structure that helps in trapping food particles.
 
• Choanocytes are essential for the sponge's filter-feeding and water circulation.
 
 
 
• **Water Canal System:**
 
 
• It consists of pathways like ostia, spongocoel, and osculum through which water flows.
 
• The system aids in nutrient absorption, gas exchange, and waste removal.
 
 
 
• **Skeleton of Sponges:**
 
 
• Sponges possess a skeleton made of **spicules (calcium carbonate or silica) or spongin fibers**.
 
• These structures provide support and protection.
 
 
 
• **Reproduction in Sponges:**
 
 
• Sponges reproduce sexually via gametes and asexually via budding or gemmules.
 
• They are mostly hermaphroditic, with both male and female reproductive cells present in the same organism.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Importance:**
 
 
• Sponges play a crucial role in marine ecosystems as filter feeders, cleaning water and recycling nutrients.
 
• They also serve as habitats for various microorganisms and small marine organisms.

questions.question: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948 aimed at:

• **Regional Imbalances:** The policy sought to reduce disparities in industrial development across different regions of the country.
 
• **Industrialization Strategy:** The resolution emphasized self-reliance and the development of heavy industries to accelerate economic growth and reduce dependency on foreign countries.

questions.question: What was the objective of the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan?

options.text: Creating jobs in the rural sector

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Achieving universal sanitation coverage**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Swachh Bharat Abhiyan (Clean India Mission) was launched by PM Narendra Modi on **2nd October 2014**, coinciding with Mahatma Gandhi's birth anniversary.
 
• The primary objective of the mission was to **achieve universal sanitation coverage** and eliminate open defecation in India.
 
• The campaign aimed to construct toilets in rural and urban areas to provide access to safe and hygienic sanitation facilities.
 
• It encouraged behavioral changes among citizens to adopt proper sanitation practices and maintain cleanliness in their surroundings.
 
• The Swachh Bharat Mission is divided into two sub-missions: **Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban)** and **Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin)**, targeting urban and rural areas respectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Open Defecation Free (ODF) Status:**

 
 
• Under the Swachh Bharat Mission, villages, towns, and cities were declared Open Defecation Free (ODF) upon achieving 100% toilet coverage.
 
• ODF+ and ODF++ statuses were introduced to focus on sustained sanitation practices and cleanliness beyond toilet construction.
 
 
 
• **Behavioral Change Campaigns:**
 
 
• The mission emphasized mass awareness campaigns to promote hygiene and sanitation.
 
• Programs like "Darwaza Band" and collaboration with celebrities were used to spread awareness regarding toilet usage.
 
 
 
• **Financial Support:**
 
 
• In rural areas, financial assistance was provided for the construction of individual household toilets under the Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin).
 
• Various state governments also supplemented central funds to ensure the success of the mission.
 
 
 
• **Impact:**
 
 
• According to government data, more than 10 crore toilets were constructed across India under the mission.
 
• The initiative significantly contributed to reducing health issues caused by poor sanitation and unhygienic practices.

questions.question: Who among the following is related to the Parakram Diwas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Subhash Bose**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Parakram Diwas is celebrated annually on **23rd January** to honor the birth anniversary of Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose.
 
• Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose was one of the most prominent leaders in India’s struggle for independence and the founder of the **Indian National Army (INA).**
 
• The Government of India declared 23rd January as Parakram Diwas in **2021** to inspire citizens with Netaji’s indomitable spirit and selfless service to the nation.
 
• Subhash Chandra Bose is remembered for his famous slogan, **"Give me blood, and I will give you freedom."**
 
• Various programs and events are organized across the country to celebrate Netaji’s contributions and legacy on Parakram Diwas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose**

 
 
• Born on **23rd January 1897** in Cuttack, Odisha, Bose was a revolutionary freedom fighter who played a pivotal role in India’s independence movement.
 
• He founded the Indian National Army (INA) in **1943** to fight against British rule in India.
 
• Netaji’s leadership and vision were instrumental in galvanizing Indians to fight for their freedom.
 
• He was associated with the **Forward Bloc**, a faction within the Indian National Congress that advocated for radical approaches to achieving independence.
 
 
 
• **Indian National Army (INA)**
 
 
• The INA was established with the help of Japan during World War II to fight against the British forces in India.
 
• It was composed of Indian prisoners of war and expatriates who believed in Netaji’s vision for a free India.
 
• The INA adopted the slogan **“Chalo Dilli”** (March to Delhi) as part of its campaign against British rule.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Netaji**
 
 
• Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose is regarded as a symbol of courage, patriotism, and leadership in Indian history.
 
• His contributions have left an indelible mark on India’s freedom struggle, and he continues to be celebrated as an icon of resistance against colonial rule.
 
• Many institutions, roads, and programs are named after Netaji to honor his legacy.

questions.question: If a soldier fires on a mob by the order of his superior officer, in conformity with the law". According to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, has he committed an offence?

options.text: Yes, because he could have disobeyed
No, because he followed public orders
No, because he believed in good faith that he was bound by law

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**No, because he believed in good faith that he was bound by law**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Under the **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023**, a person acting under the legal orders of a superior officer is generally exempted from criminal liability.
 
• The soldier, in this case, acted in **good faith** under the belief that he was bound by law to follow the orders of his superior.
 
• The principle of "good faith" protects individuals who reasonably believe that their actions are lawful when following superior orders.
 
• The law emphasizes that such actions are not punishable if performed in **compliance with legal orders** and without personal malice.
 
• This principle is rooted in the legal doctrine of immunity for acts committed under lawful authority, ensuring discipline in hierarchical systems such as the military.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Good Faith:**

 
 
• It refers to an honest intention to act without taking an unfair advantage over another party.
 
• In legal contexts, actions taken in good faith are often exempt from liability if performed under lawful authority.
 
 
 
• **Superior Orders:**
 
 
• Also known as the "Nuremberg Defense," it is a legal doctrine where individuals claim they are not responsible for actions performed under orders from a superior.
 
• Indian law accepts this defense only when the orders are lawful and the individual acts in good faith.
 
 
 
• **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023:**
 
 
• This is the proposed replacement for the Indian Penal Code (IPC), aiming to modernize criminal laws in India.
 
• It emphasizes accountability, fairness, and adherence to the rule of law.
 
 
 
• **Military Discipline:**
 
 
• Discipline in the armed forces is maintained through strict adherence to lawful orders.
 
• The exemption for acts performed in good faith under superior orders ensures operational efficiency without compromising legality.

questions.question: High honey yield and gentle behaviour in bees for commercial beekeeping can be achieved through one of the following methods:

options.text: Using wild bee species with aggressive defence traits

__
 
• **Italian bees (Apis mellifera ligustica)** are known for their high honey yield and gentle behavior, making them ideal for commercial beekeeping.
 
• These bees have a **longer foraging period** and are less prone to abandoning their hives, ensuring consistent honey production.
 
• Italian bees exhibit **low aggression**, making them easier to manage compared to wild or native bee species with aggressive defense mechanisms.
 
• They are widely used in commercial beekeeping due to their **efficient colony management** and ability to adapt well to diverse environmental conditions.
 
• The introduction of such bees enhances both **honey production** and overall profitability for beekeepers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Apis mellifera ligustica (Italian bees):**

 
 
• Italian bees are a subspecies of the western honeybee (Apis mellifera) and are native to Italy.
 
• They are characterized by their **golden-yellow coloration** and calm temperament.
 
• They are preferred globally in apiculture due to their efficient honey production and resistance to certain diseases.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Bee Behavior in Beekeeping:**
 
 
• Gentle behavior in bees reduces the risk of stings, making hive management safer for beekeepers.
 
• Non-aggressive species are easier to handle during hive inspections and honey extraction processes.
 
 
 
• **Commercial Beekeeping Practices:**
 
 
• Beekeepers often select bee species that exhibit traits such as high honey yield, disease resistance, and adaptability to local climates.
 
• Proper hive management, pest control, and regular monitoring are essential for maintaining healthy bee colonies.
 
 
 
• **Economic Significance of Beekeeping:**
 
 
• Beekeeping contributes significantly to agriculture through **pollination services**, improving crop yields.
 
• It provides a sustainable source of income for rural communities through the sale of honey, beeswax, and other by-products.

questions.question: Who headed the Credentials Committee in the Constituent Assembly?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alladi Krishnaswamy Aiyar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Alladi Krishnaswamy Aiyar was an eminent lawyer and jurist who played a key role in the drafting of India's Constitution.
 
• He headed the Credentials Committee in the Constituent Assembly, a critical committee tasked with verifying the credentials of members.
 
• Aiyar was also a member of the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution, chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
 
• Known for his deep legal expertise, Aiyar contributed significantly to the formulation of constitutional provisions.
 
• His contributions were instrumental in ensuring the smooth functioning of the Constituent Assembly during India's constitutional drafting process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constituent Assembly of India:**

 
 
• Formed in 1946, the Constituent Assembly was tasked with drafting the Constitution of India.
 
• It comprised representatives from various provinces and princely states of India.
 
• The Assembly had multiple committees, including the Drafting Committee, Union Powers Committee, and Credentials Committee.
 
 
 
• **Drafting Committee:**
 
 
• Chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, this committee was responsible for preparing the final draft of the Constitution.
 
• It consisted of seven members, including Alladi Krishnaswamy Aiyar, K.M. Munshi, and N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar.
 
 
 
• **Alladi Krishnaswamy Aiyar:**
 
 
• Born in 1882, Aiyar was a distinguished lawyer and served as Advocate General of Madras.
 
• He was known for his expertise in constitutional law and played a pivotal role in shaping India's legal framework.
 
 
 
• **Credentials Committee:**
 
 
• One of the smaller committees in the Constituent Assembly, it was responsible for verifying the legitimacy of Assembly members.
 
• Its work ensured that all members were duly elected or nominated as per the rules governing the Assembly.

questions.question: Which of the following is a prominent form of Hindustani classical vocal music?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dhrupad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dhrupad** is one of the oldest and most prominent forms of Hindustani classical vocal music.
 
• It traces its roots back to the **Samaveda**, one of the ancient Hindu scriptures, which contained melodic chants.
 
• This vocal style is characterized by its emphasis on purity of notes and disciplined melodic progression.
 
• Dhrupad is performed in two parts: **Alap** (a slow and elaborate introduction) and **Bandish** (the composition set to a rhythmic cycle).
 
• Renowned Dhrupad vocalists include the **Dagar family**, who played a pivotal role in preserving and propagating this art form.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hindustani Classical Music**

 
 
• It is one of the two main traditions of Indian classical music, alongside Carnatic music.
 
• Hindustani music emphasizes improvisation and exploration of ragas (melodic frameworks).
 
• It has evolved over centuries, incorporating influences from Persian and Mughal music traditions.
 
 
 
• **Samaveda**
 
 
• One of the four Vedas, Samaveda is dedicated to chants and melodies.
 
• It is considered the foundational text for Indian musical traditions, including Dhrupad.
 
 
 
• **Ragas in Dhrupad**
 
 
• Dhrupad compositions are based on specific ragas, which define the melodic structure.
 
• These ragas are performed in a meditative and disciplined manner.
 
 
 
• **Instruments Used**
 
 
• Dhrupad performances are often accompanied by the **pakhawaj** (a barrel-shaped drum) and the tanpura (a stringed instrument).
 
• These instruments add rhythm and resonance to the vocal renditions.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a primary factor affecting the variation of Insolation on Earth?

options.text: Presence of water bodies in an area
Rotation of the Earth on its axis
Angle of inclination of the Sun's rays

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Presence of water bodies in an area**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Insolation** refers to the amount of solar radiation received by the Earth's surface.
 
• The variation in insolation is primarily determined by factors such as the **angle of the Sun’s rays, Earth’s rotation, and atmospheric transparency**.
 
• The **angle of inclination of the Sun’s rays** impacts the intensity and distribution of solar energy, with higher angles resulting in more concentrated energy.
 
• The **rotation of the Earth** causes daily variations in insolation, leading to the alternation of day and night.
 
• **Transparency of the atmosphere** affects how much solar energy reaches the surface, as clouds, dust, and pollutants can block or scatter sunlight.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Primary Factors Affecting Insolation:**

 
 
• The Earth’s axial tilt (~23.5°) causes seasonal variations in insolation.
 
• The Earth's shape, being an oblate spheroid, results in uneven solar energy distribution.
 
• Latitude influences insolation, with regions near the equator receiving more consistent and intense solar energy.
 
 
 
• **Earth’s Atmosphere and Insolation:**
 
 
• The atmosphere filters solar radiation, absorbing harmful UV rays through the ozone layer.
 
• Cloud cover and atmospheric conditions such as aerosols influence the amount of insolation reaching the Earth’s surface.
 
 
 
• **Solar Constant:**
 
 
• The solar constant is the average amount of solar energy received per unit area at the top of the Earth's atmosphere, approximately **1,366 watts per square meter**.
 
• It provides a reference for understanding energy input from the Sun.
 
 
 
• **Factors NOT Primarily Affecting Insolation:**
 
 
• The presence of water bodies affects local climate and heat retention but does not directly influence the variation of insolation.
 
• Topography and vegetation also modify local heating but are secondary factors in insolation variation.

questions.question: According to Keynesian theory, during recession, what should the government ideally do?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Increasing spending and cutting taxes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Keynesian economics emphasizes the role of government intervention during economic downturns to stimulate demand and achieve full employment.
 
• In a recession, the government should increase public spending on infrastructure, education, and other sectors to create jobs and boost economic activity.
 
• Cutting taxes increases disposable income, encouraging consumers to spend more, which in turn drives demand.
 
• By combining increased government spending and tax cuts, the Keynesian approach aims to close the output gap and restore economic stability.
 
• This counter-cyclical fiscal policy helps to counteract the effects of reduced private sector spending during a recession.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Keynesian Economics:**

 
 
• Developed by John Maynard Keynes, it argues that aggregate demand is the primary driver of economic growth and employment.
 
• Keynes advocated for active government intervention in the economy, particularly during periods of economic downturns.
 
• It opposes the idea of self-regulating markets, emphasizing that markets may fail to recover quickly without external support.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal Policy:**
 
 
• Fiscal policy refers to government spending and taxation policies used to influence economic conditions.
 
• Expansionary fiscal policy involves increased government spending and tax reductions, often employed during recessions.
 
 
 
• **Multiplier Effect:**
 
 
• In Keynesian theory, the multiplier effect highlights how an initial increase in spending leads to a greater overall increase in economic output.
 
• For example, government spending on infrastructure creates jobs, which increases consumer spending, further stimulating demand.
 
 
 
• **Automatic Stabilizers:**
 
 
• These are economic policies and programs, such as unemployment benefits and progressive taxation, that automatically adjust to stabilize the economy during fluctuations.
 
• They help reduce the severity of recessions without requiring direct government intervention.
 
 
 
• **Criticism of Keynesian Economics:**
 
 
• Critics argue that excessive government spending can lead to high public debt and inflation.
 
• Others believe that reliance on fiscal policy may crowd out private sector investment.

• The SpaDex mission aims to test advanced guidance, navigation, and control systems necessary for precise docking maneuvers in space.
 
• Successful space docking is critical for assembling large spacecraft, transferring cargo, and enabling long-duration missions in deep space.
 
• SpaDex contributes to advancing space exploration capabilities, making future missions more efficient and reliable.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Space Docking:**

 
 
• Space docking is a critical operation where two spacecraft connect while in orbit, enabling crew transfers and resource sharing.
 
• It has been used in missions involving the International Space Station (ISS), Apollo-Soyuz Test Project, and SpaceX Crew Dragon.
 
• Docking requires precise alignment and synchronization of speed and trajectory between the docking spacecraft.
 
 
 
• **Autonomous Docking Systems:**

• These systems reduce human intervention, making docking safer and more efficient for future space missions.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Docking Technology:**

questions.question:
which of the following systems can be affected by a solar storm?

1. GPS signal accuracy

2. Power transmission systems

3. Submarine communication cables

4. Pipeline infrastructure
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1,2,3, and 4 all of these**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **GPS signal accuracy:** Solar storms can disrupt satellite signals by affecting the ionosphere, leading to inaccuracies in GPS systems.
 
• **Power transmission systems:** Geomagnetic storms induced by solar activity can cause fluctuations in Earth's magnetic field, affecting power grids and leading to outages.
 
• **Submarine communication cables:** Solar storms can interfere with undersea communication systems by inducing geomagnetic currents, impacting data transmission.
 
• **Pipeline infrastructure:** Variations in Earth's magnetic field caused by solar storms can induce currents in pipelines, leading to corrosion and operational challenges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solar storms:** These are disturbances on the sun’s surface that release large amounts of charged particles, electromagnetic radiation, and magnetic fields into space.
 
• **Geomagnetic storms:** When solar storms interact with Earth's magnetic field, they can lead to geomagnetic storms, impacting satellites, power grids, and communication systems.
 
• **Ionosphere effects:** Solar activity alters the ionosphere, a layer of Earth's atmosphere that plays a key role in radio communication and GPS signal propagation.
 
• **Corrosion in pipelines:** Geomagnetically induced currents during solar storms accelerate corrosion in pipelines, affecting their longevity and efficiency.
 
• **Space weather monitoring:** Agencies like NASA and NOAA continuously monitor solar activity and issue alerts to mitigate risks associated with solar storms.
